text.p: Philip Geier, Jr., chairman of the board and chief executive officer at Interpublic Group of Cos Inc, said Thursday the company's financial condition "continues to be excellent, with a strong balance sheet and a solid cash position."

Interpublic said in a release that continuing cost containment efforts have kept costs at "appropriate levels" and that the company's agency systems "gained record net new business" during the first three months of 1997.
The company said it gained about $472 million of billings for the first three months of 1997, compared with $411 million of billings for the first three months of 1996, an increase of 15 percent.
Interpublic reported net income for the first quarter of 1997 of about $22 million, an increase of 23.6 percent over net income for the first quarter of 1996 of $17.8 million.
Earnings per share increased 17 percent to $0.27 from $0.23 for the comparable period of 1996, it added.
Gross income for the first quarter of 1997 was $597.2 million, an increase of $91.1 million or 18 percent over 1996, the company said.
It added that gross income from U.S. operations increased 35.3 percent and gross income from international operations was up 6.9 percent.
The company said gross income from international operations would have been up 13.2 percent, except for strengthening of the U.S. dollar against major currencies.
